newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear plans upgrade for S.African facility.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear plans upgrade for S.African facility.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co plans to invest $20 million in the next 18 months to upgrade and modernize a South African plant in which it plans to re-acquire an interest, chairman Samir Gibara said Monday.
The Akron, Ohio-based tiremaker at this time does not plan to add or lay off workers there, said Gibara, interviewed by telephone from South Africa. The stock was off 5/8 to 48-7/8.
Earlier Monday Goodyear said it agreed to acquire a 60 percent interest in the Contred tire/engineered products unit of Consol Ltd for $121 million including assumed debt.

Consol parent Anglovaal Industries Ltd will retain 40 percent although Goodyear may buy that stake within five years, Gibara said. Goodyear said the deal is valued at about 568 million South African rand and will close January 1.
It includes a tire and engineered products factory which Goodyear built in 1947 in Uitenhage, Cape Province. It also includes 195 retail stores and a retreading operation.
"(We plan) to invest ... in the next 18 months another $20 million to upgrade the plant and modernize it," Gibara said.
In 1989 when many U.S. companies were divesting in South Africa due to apartheid, Goodyear sold to the Anglovaal group.
Consol retained a licensing agreement with Goodyear.

"We've had an ongoing relationship with the Anglovaal (group)," said Gibara, who is also is president and chief executive officer. "They approached us recently and asked us if we would be interested in going back."

Analyst Harry Millis of Fundamental Research, Willoughby, Ohio, said South Africa has always been a strong market for Goodyear. "They have an excellent reputation in South Africa and I think it makes sense to capitalize on it," Millis said.
Gibara said Goodyear will rationalize production with other manufacturing plants, mainly in Europe.
That is, the Uitenhage plant will make more tires but in fewer sizes; some sizes will be imported to South Africa while some South African-made tires will be exported, he said.

"On the tire side, the opportunity is for us to export from South Africa to the rest of Africa, where we traditionally have not had a very good market share," particularly in sub-Saharan countries, he said.

The plant also makes conveyor belts, which it supplies to "many, many mines" in Africa, Gibara said, adding he sees opportunities to increase that business as well. Goodyear will maintain job training and black community programs, he said.
